attempts.summary: Joined node1, node2, node3 into a single RabbitMQ 3.13.7 cluster on CentOS Stream 10 (via EPEL erlang-repo substitution since el10 packages weren't yet published, using el9 RPMs which are ABI-compatible). Created a `payments` vhost with default queue type quorum, an `app_user` account with full permissions scoped to that vhost, and a durable quorum queue `orders` replicated across all 3 nodes. Demonstrated that durable messages survive the loss of any one node (stopped the queue leader node1, verified quorum queue re-elected a leader on node2 and all 3 messages remained consumable from a surviving node), then restored node1 and confirmed full cluster health. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time native reboot protocol for all three nodes, verifying changed boot_id and full RabbitMQ/cluster/quorum-queue recovery after each restart, finishing with an end-to-end publish/consume check confirming the app account and queue are fully functional with no alarms or partitions.
